An octopus has three hearts. And one of them stops beating every time it swims.
That sounds like a design mistake. It is actually the reason octopuses walk.
Start with the plumbing. Two small hearts sit next to the gills. Their only job is to push blood through the gills to pick up oxygen.
The third heart is bigger. It takes that fresh blood and sends it to the rest of the body.
Here is the catch. When an octopus swims by jet propulsion, the big heart pauses. No fresh blood reaches the muscles.
So swimming wears it out in seconds. Crawling keeps all three hearts working, which is why an octopus would rather walk across the sea floor.
